source_authority: Published product documentation; not adopted project policy
span_convention: One-based inclusive lines; SHA-256 of UTF-8 lines joined by LF without trailing LF. Every span is verified separately in both complete bodies; version-prefixed dependency links are excluded from shared spans.

claims.statement: The described feature is in public preview.
Preview functionality can change.
Desktop interaction is described as capability context, not a mandate to enable the feature.
The availability described here applies to local macOS and Windows sessions.
The settings route enables the feature in the app's Computer Use section.
On macOS, Accessibility permission enables application-control interaction.
On macOS, Screen Recording permission enables visual inspection when needed.
If a permission change is not detected on macOS, use the prerequisite recheck control.
The session on command is an alternate enablement entry point.
The session status command reports plugin and MCP status, not proof of effective application access.
Requests should specify the desired outcome.
Requests should specify the involved applications.
Requests should specify important constraints.
The app Tool Permissions setting governs application-control approval prompting.
Review or change tool permission settings in the app's Sessions settings section.
When prompted, check that the requested application matches the intended task.
When prompted, check that the requested action matches the intended task.
Allow grants application access for the current computer-use session.
Always allow saves approval for future sessions.
The operator can decline or cancel an approval request.
Stop interrupts the current app operation.
One Escape press is an alternate app-operation interrupt, distinct from the CLI two-press instruction.
Persistent grants originating in either app or CLI apply to both surfaces on the same computer.
Saved application grants can be removed individually from the Always allowed apps list.
Removing a saved grant changes future-session approval in both app and CLI.
Removing a saved grant does not revoke application access already granted to a running session.
Stopping a current operation is distinct from ending its session.
End the session to revoke application access granted to that session, according to the source.
The app settings toggle provides feature disablement.
The session off command is an alternate feature-disablement route; the cited span does not establish persistent-grant deletion.
If settings are unavailable, confirm account feature availability.
If settings are unavailable, confirm operating-system feature availability.
For macOS troubleshooting, verify Accessibility actually reports granted under prerequisites.
For macOS troubleshooting, verify Screen Recording separately reports granted under prerequisites.
